description:
Audit events must include the client source IP. Currently basic_auth_middleware has no access to the peer address. Add source IP extraction as a prerequisite for audit event instrumentation.

## What to do
  1. Add axum::extract::ConnectInfo<SocketAddr> to the server startup in main.rs:
       TcpListener::bind(addr).await?
       axum::serve(listener, router.into_make_service_with_connect_info::<SocketAddr>())
     (Currently uses into_make_service() which does not populate ConnectInfo.)

  2. In basic_auth_middleware extract the peer address:
       let source_ip = req
           .extensions()
           .get::<ConnectInfo<SocketAddr>>()
           .map(|ci| ci.0.ip().to_string())
           .unwrap_or_else(|| "-".to_string());

  3. Behind a load balancer, the direct peer is the LB. Add support for
     X-Forwarded-For and X-Real-IP headers as fallback, gated on a config
     flag (trust_proxy = false by default to prevent spoofing when running
     without a proxy). Only the first value in XFF is used.

  4. Forward source_ip into the request extensions so downstream handlers
     (and audit log calls) can read it without re-extracting.

## Why trust_proxy must default false
If trust_proxy = true on a server directly exposed to the internet,
an attacker can forge X-Forwarded-For to spoof any IP in audit logs.
This is a known audit log poisoning vector. Default to false; operators
set it to true only when behind a trusted proxy.

## Acceptance
- Unit test: request with ConnectInfo populated → source_ip = actual IP
- Unit test: trust_proxy=true + X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4 → source_ip = 1.2.3.4
- Unit test: trust_proxy=false + X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4 → source_ip = actual peer IP
title: Extract and forward client source IP through auth middleware
